1	# Plan
     2	
     3	## Plan Audit Cycles
     4	- Audits: none — Plan Auditor v1.7.0
     5	- Architectural Reviews: 1 — Plan Architect Reviewer v2.2.0
     6	
     7	## Summary
     8	
     9	This plan delivers two tightly related features that share the same goal — making LangGraph agent dialogue readable without parsing raw JSONL:
    10	
    11	1. **CLI extraction script** (`scripts/extract-dialogue.js`): A standalone Node.js script that reads chunk `.jsonl` files, assembles the streaming message fragments into complete prose turns, and writes a Markdown `.md` file alongside the source. Supports single-file and directory batch modes. Callable by the Orchestrator Archaeologist and developers directly.
    12	
    13	2. **GUI "Text Only" tab**: When viewing a dialogue chunk in the MCP Server GUI, the dialogue modal gains a two-tab layout — **Detailed** (the current interactive structured view) and **Text Only** (extracted prose). The text is fetched from a new backend endpoint that either reads an existing cached `.md` file or extracts and writes one on first access. Both the CLI and the GUI produce the same `.md` format, so either can prime the cache.
    14	
    15	The Archaeologist persona source is updated to replace the "(future)" placeholder with a concrete reference to both tools.
    16	
    17	---
    18	
    19	## Architectural Context
    20	
    21	The orchestrator saves one JSONL chunk file per agent stage run under `{slug}/orchestrator/chunks/`. Each file is a stream of LangGraph `AIMessageChunk` and `ToolMessage` objects serialized as JSONL. The streaming nature means a single AI response turn is split across dozens to hundreds of lines, and tool call arguments are fragmented into `input_json_delta` partial-JSON strings. The files are currently analysed by the Orchestrator Archaeologist by reading raw lines — a laborious process.
    22	
    23	The MCP Server GUI already has a rich chunk-viewing facility: `mcp-server/gui/chunk-renderer.ts` contains `renderChunksToMarkdown()`, `renderChunksToDialogue()`, and `renderChunksToStructured()` — pure rendering functions that accumulate streaming fragments into merged messages and produce human-readable output. These are served via the `GET /api/projects/:repo/:slug/chunks/:filename/rendered` endpoint in `server.ts`. The existing dialogue modal in `project-detail-dialogues.js` uses the structured renderer to produce an interactive view with collapsible tool-call cards.
    24	
    25	CLI scripts follow the pattern established by `scripts/read-log.js`: pure Node.js ESM, stdlib-only, CLI-first with a `--help` flag, invokable via `node scripts/<name>.js` or through `scripts/cli.js`.
    26	
    27	---
    28	
    29	## Approach / Architecture
    30	
    31	The solution has two interacting parts that share the same `.md` output format:
    32	
    33	### Part 1 — CLI extraction script (`scripts/extract-dialogue.js`)
    34	
    35	A standalone Node.js ESM script that accepts a chunk file path or directory. It:
    36	1. Parses each JSONL chunk file in a single pass, assembling streaming fragments by run ID and tool-call index into complete turns.
    37	2. Separates dialogue by namespace depth: outer/sole agent (`ns.length === 0`, empty namespace array) and inner agent (`ns.length > 0`). Single-depth files render flat; dual-depth files render two labelled sections.
    38	3. Outputs **prose text only** (no tool-call JSON, no tool results) — the agent's reasoning in readable paragraphs.
    39	4. Writes a `.md` file in the same directory as the source `.jsonl` (same base name). Skips existing files unless `--force` is passed.
    40	
    41	### Part 2 — GUI "Text Only" tab
    42	
    43	The dialogue modal in `project-detail-dialogues.js` gains a tab bar (only when `useChunks === true`):
    44	- **Detailed** tab: the existing structured block renderer (interactive, tool-call toggles). Default active.
    45	- **Text Only** tab: prose-only Markdown view, lazily loaded on first tab click.
    46	
    47	The backend serves the "Text Only" content via a new endpoint `GET /api/projects/:repo/:slug/chunks/:filename/text` that:
    48	1. Checks for an existing `.md` file next to the `.jsonl` in the chunk directory.
    49	2. If found (CLI pre-generated or prior GUI access): reads and returns it directly.
    50	3. If not found: calls the new `renderChunksToText()` renderer (TypeScript, server-side), writes the `.md` file as a side-effect (best-effort caching), and returns the content.
    51	
    52	This design means the CLI and the GUI share the same cache file — whichever runs first primes it for the other.
    53	
    54	### Shared `.md` output format
    55	
    56	Both the CLI and the server-side `renderChunksToText()` produce the same format: plain prose paragraphs only (AI text content), no tool calls. For dual-namespace files, sections are labelled:
    57	```markdown
    58	## Outer Agent
    59	
    60	<prose>
    61	
    62	## Inner Agent
    63	
    64	<prose>
    65	```
    66	For single-namespace files: no section headers, just prose paragraphs.
    67	
    68	---
    69	
    70	## Rationale
    71	
    72	**CLI approach:** Placing the extractor in `scripts/` alongside `read-log.js` keeps it discoverable and consistent. Writing `.md` files alongside `.jsonl` files (same directory, same base name) makes it trivially easy to open the readable version without a separate output path. Assembling streaming chunks in a single pass is sufficient — the files are small enough to fit in memory.
    73	
    74	**GUI tab approach:** Adding a second tab to the existing modal is the least disruptive UI change — the Detailed view is unchanged. Lazy-loading the text tab means no extra network request for users who never need it. Caching as a `.md` file means repeated access is instant and the file is also available from the CLI.
    75	
    76	**Shared `.md` format:** A prose-only output (no tool-call JSON) is the right content for "Text Only" — it serves the debugging use case of reading the agent's actual reasoning, not its tool invocations (which the Detailed tab already shows). The CLI and GUI write the same format so the cache is cross-tool compatible.
    77	
    78	**Server-side renderer vs. CLI sharing code:** The server-side `renderChunksToText()` lives in TypeScript and cannot be imported by the standalone Node.js CLI script without a build step. Both implement the same algorithm independently. The format contract (described above) ensures compatible output.
    79	
    80	---
    81	
    82	## Considered Alternatives
    83	
    84	| Decision | Chosen Shape | Alternatives Considered | Trade-Off Summary |
    85	|----------|--------------|-------------------------|-------------------|
    86	| Output location | `.md` alongside `.jsonl` (same dir, same stem) | Separate `--output-dir`, stdout | Co-location makes it obvious; stdout would not save files as required; separate dir adds indirection |
    87	| Text only content | Prose text only (no tool calls) | Full dialogue (text + tool summaries) | "Text Only" should be the agent's reasoning, not its tool calls; Detailed tab already covers the full interactive view |
    88	| Inner/outer rendering | Separate sections when both depths present | Always separate, always merged | Merged output for single-depth files avoids empty sections; dual-depth files genuinely have two distinct agent levels |
    89	| Arg assembly in CLI | Index-based accumulation of `tool_call_chunks[].args` | Use `msg.tool_calls[].args` from final chunk | Index-based approach verified correct on real data; `tool_calls.args` remains `{}` throughout streaming |
    90	| CLI skip/overwrite default | Skip existing `.md` by default, `--force` to overwrite | Always overwrite | Skipping protects hand-annotated output; `--force` provides an easy override |
    91	| CLI registration in cli.js | `helpHidden: true`, `key: null` | Interactive menu entry | Matches the `read-log` pattern for secondary tooling; not needed in the main interactive menu |
    92	| GUI tab placement | Below header, above body (separate `.dialogue-modal-tabs` div) | Tabs inside header; content-toggle buttons | Keeps header clean (title + close always visible); tab bar is its own layout row consistent with standard tab UI patterns |
    93	| GUI text loading | Lazy (fetched on first tab click) | Eager (fetch both tabs on modal open) | Lazy avoids a wasted request when user only needs the Detailed view (the common case) |
    94	| Server-side `.md` write | Best-effort (ignore write errors, always return content) | Hard-fail on write error | Write errors (permissions, disk) should not break the read path; content is always returned regardless |
    95	| Code sharing between CLI and server | Independent implementations sharing a format contract | CLI imports from compiled dist | The compiled dist may be stale; an independent pure-JS implementation avoids build coupling |
    96	
    97	---
    98	
    99	## Pattern Alignment

   124	1. **Add `renderChunksToText()` to `mcp-server/gui/chunk-renderer.ts`**:
   125	   - Add a private helper `extractTextFromMessages(messages: MergedMessage[]): string` that iterates AI messages (type `ai`/`aimessage`/`aimessagechunk`), calls `renderContent(msg.content).trim()` on each, and joins non-empty results with `'\n\n'`.
   126	   - Add a public exported function `renderChunksToText(jsonlContent: string): string`:
   127	     - Call `parseJsonlContent(jsonlContent)` then `accumulateChunks(records)` (both already exist).
   128	     - Detect whether any namespace key is non-empty (i.e. sub-agents are present: `[...nsMap.keys()].some(k => k !== '')`).
   129	     - If **no sub-agents**: extract text from the main namespace (`nsMap.get('')`) and return it directly.
   130	     - If **sub-agents present**: prefix the main namespace text with `'## Outer Agent\n\n'` and each sub-agent namespace with `'## Inner Agent\n\n'` (the `namespaceLabel()` helper is available for the label). Concatenate with blank-line separators.
   131	     - Return the joined text terminated with `'\n'`. Return `'*No dialogue recorded.*\n'` when `nsMap.size === 0` or all text is empty.
   132	   - Export `renderChunksToText` from the module's public API (alongside the existing three renderers).
   133	
   134	### Part 2 — Backend API handler and route
   135	
   136	2. **Add `handleGetChunkText()` to `mcp-server/gui/api.ts`**:
   137	   - Add `writeFile` to the existing `import { rm, readFile, readdir } from 'node:fs/promises'` import.
   138	   - Implement `handleGetChunkText(ledgerRoot, slug, filename, repoName?)`:
   139	     - `assertSafeSlug(slug)`.
   140	     - `if (!CHUNK_FILENAME_RE.test(filename))` → `notFound(...)`.
   141	     - `resolveProjectStore(ledgerRoot, slug, repoName)` to get `store.storageDir`.
   142	     - Compute `chunksDir = resolve(join(store.storageDir, CHUNKS_DIR))`.
   143	     - Compute `mdFilename = filename.replace(/\.jsonl$/, '.md')` and `mdPath = resolve(join(chunksDir, mdFilename))`.
   144	     - Path-prefix check on `mdPath` (defence-in-depth).
   145	     - Try to `readFile(mdPath, 'utf-8')` — if it succeeds, return `{ content, cached: true }`.
   146	     - If `ENOENT`: read the `.jsonl` via `readFile(resolve(join(chunksDir, filename)), 'utf-8')` (with its own `ENOENT` → `notFound` guard).
   147	     - Call `renderChunksToText(chunkContent)`.
   148	     - Best-effort `writeFile(mdPath, textContent, 'utf-8')` wrapped in try/catch (ignore errors).
   149	     - Return `{ content: textContent, cached: false }`.
   150	   - Import `renderChunksToText` from `'./chunk-renderer.js'` (`api.ts` lives in `mcp-server/gui/` — same directory as `chunk-renderer.ts`; a `../gui/` prefix would be wrong).

1	# Orchestrator Archaeologist
     2	
     3	## Mission
     4	
     5	**Identity: Forensic Operations Analyst.**
     6	
     7	Excavate stored orchestrator run artifacts — structured JSONL logs and raw dialogue chunk files — to identify technical issues, friction points, and behavioral anomalies that occurred during LangGraph Deep Agents pipeline execution. Produce an actionable diagnostic report that surfaces what went wrong, what was inefficient, and what patterns indicate systemic problems in the virtualization layer.
     8	
     9	---
    10	
    11	## Operating Philosophy
    12	
    13	- **Artifacts Tell the Truth.** Agent self-reports are aspirational; timestamps, error codes, and token counts are factual. Prefer quantitative signals (duration spikes, token waste, retry counts) over narrative claims in dialogue chunks.
    14	- **Silence Is a Signal.** Long heartbeat gaps, missing expected events, and absent chunk files are as diagnostic as explicit errors. A 5-minute heartbeat gap during a stage that completed in 30 seconds elsewhere reveals a stall the agent never mentioned.
    15	- **Patterns Over Incidents.** A single stage error is an anecdote. The same error class appearing across multiple WPs or runs is a systemic issue. Prioritize findings that recur or compound.
    16	- **Context Preserves Meaning.** An isolated `stage_error` is noise without the preceding `tool_call` sequence and routing decision that led to it. Always reconstruct the causal chain before classifying a finding.
    17	
    18	---
    19	
    20	## Inputs
    21	
    22	You will be provided with:
    23	
    24	- **Orchestrator Directory:** The `orchestrator/` subdirectory within a ledger project folder, containing `logs/` and `chunks/` subdirectories.
    25	- **Optional: Specific Focus Area.** The user may narrow the investigation to a specific WP, stage, or concern (e.g., "Why did WP-002 take so long?" or "Check for rework loops").
    26	- **Optional: Comparison Baseline.** A second orchestrator directory from another run for comparative analysis.
    27	
    28	### Capabilities
    29	
    30	- **Filesystem Access:** Read log and chunk JSONL files within the provided orchestrator directory. Read the project's `project-ledger.json` and WP artifacts for cross-referencing when needed.
    31	- **CLI Tool Access:** Use `node scripts/extract-dialogue.js <chunk-file>` to extract prose text from a chunk `.jsonl` file into a readable `.md` file alongside it — no tool-call JSON, no tool results, just the agent's reasoning text. Use `node scripts/extract-dialogue.js <directory>` to batch-extract all `.jsonl` files in a directory. When a project is open in the MCP GUI, the **"Text Only"** tab on each chunk dialogue modal renders the same prose extraction inline without writing any file. Fall back to raw JSONL reads when neither option is available.
    32	
    33	---
    34	
    35	## Outputs
    36	
    37	A structured **Orchestrator Diagnostic Report** delivered inline. The report contains a run overview, a timeline reconstruction, categorized findings with severity ratings, and actionable recommendations.
    38	
    39	---
    40	
    41	## Reference Material
    42	
    43	### Orchestrator File Layout
    44	
    45	```
    46	{slug}/orchestrator/
    47	├── logs/
    48	│   └── {timestamp}-{slug}.jsonl          # Structured run log (one per run)
    49	└── chunks/
    50	    ├── project-pm-r{N}.jsonl             # PM stage dialogue (project-level)
    51	    ├── project-synthesis-r{N}.jsonl      # Synthesis stage dialogue
    52	    ├── {WP-ID}-developer-r{N}.jsonl      # Developer stage per WP
    53	    ├── {WP-ID}-qa-r{N}.jsonl             # QA stage per WP
    54	    ├── {WP-ID}-reviewer-r{N}.jsonl       # Reviewer stage per WP
    55	    └── {WP-ID}-docs-r{N}.jsonl           # Docs stage per WP
    56	```
    57	
    58	Revision numbers (`r0`, `r1`, …) auto-increment; the highest `r` suffix is the most recent run of that stage.
    59	
    60	### Log File Schema (JSONL)
    61	
    62	Each line in the log file is a JSON object. Key fields:
    63	
    64	| Field | Description |
    65	|-------|-------------|
    66	| `timestamp` | ISO 8601 UTC wall-clock time |
    67	| `stage` | Node name: `"cli"`, `"supervisor"`, `"developer"`, `"qa"`, `"pm"`, etc. |
    68	| `wp_id` | Work package being processed (empty string for project-level events) |
    69	| `action` | Event type — see Action Catalog below |
    70	| `result` | `"PASS"` or `"FAIL"` (stage completion events only) |
    71	| `level` | `"INFO"`, `"WARNING"`, `"ERROR"`, `"DEBUG"` |
    72	| `error` | Error message (present only on error-level events) |
    73	| `tokens_used` | `{input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens}` (stage_complete only) |
    74	| `duration_s` | Wallclock seconds for the stage or pipeline |
    75	| `model` | API model slug used (e.g., `"claude-sonnet-4-6"`) |
    76	| `tool_name` | MCP tool name (tool_call events only) |
    77	| `silence_s` | Seconds since last log entry (heartbeat events only) |
    78	
    79	### Action Catalog — Diagnostic Priority
    80	
    81	**High-value diagnostic events** (always investigate):
    82	
    83	| Action | Meaning |
    84	|--------|---------|
    85	| `stage_error` | Agent stage crashed — `result="FAIL"`, check `error` field |
    86	| `mcp_error` | MCP server returned an error to the supervisor |
    87	| `rework_detected` | A pipeline was bounced back for rework |
    88	| `halted_repeated_failure` | WP halted after consecutive failures — circuit breaker skips it |
    89	| `halted_wp_cancelled` | Circuit-broken WP auto-cancelled so synthesis can proceed |
    90	| `safety_limit` | Supervisor hit the iteration ceiling |
    91	| `pipeline_rollback` | An orphaned in-progress pipeline was rolled back |
    92	| `stage_retry` | Transient API error triggered a retry |
    93	| `signal_shutdown` | Run was interrupted by SIGTERM/SIGINT |
    94	
    95	**Contextual events** (needed to reconstruct the timeline):
    96	
    97	| Action | Meaning |
    98	|--------|---------|
    99	| `run_start` | Run began — carries `thread_id`, `stage_models`, `plan` path |
   100	| `run_end` | Run finished — carries `result` and `total_duration_s` |

1	﻿# Public API Surface
     2	
     3	This document lists **public constructors, properties, and method signatures** for all exported classes, functions, and types. Implementation details are omitted.
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## MCP Tools (30 Total)
     8	
     9	The primary public API is the set of **MCP tools** registered by the server. Agents invoke these tools via the MCP protocol.
    10	
    11	### Project Lifecycle Tools
    12	
    13	#### `ledger_get_project_status`
    14	
    15	```typescript
    16	(args: { project_path?: string; cwd_path?: string }) => Promise<MCPResult>
    17	// Note: provide cwd_path (workspace root, preferred — auto-detects project) or project_path (fallback — use only if already known).
    18	```
    19	
    20	Reads the root index and returns project overview. Includes self-healing logic (`computeHealedStatus`) that recomputes counters and status from actual work package data. Self-healing separates computation (pure function) from persistence (conditional write under lock). No disk write occurs if counters and status are already correct.
    21	
    22	When a write is triggered, the write callback calls `clearSynthesisState(fresh)` if `corruptionDetected` is true (i.e. synthesis was flagged prematurely while pending WPs still exist). `validatePipelineOrdering` runs outside the lock (it only reads WP detail files) and its warnings are applied inside the consolidated lock scope along with all other repairs.
    23	
    24	**Legacy field repair (self-healing on read):** In addition to status and counter healing, `getProjectStatus` performs two legacy-field repair passes on every call:
    25	
    26	1. **`synthesis_generated_at` backfill:** If `synthesis_generated === true` and `synthesis_generated_at` is absent or `null` and `corruptionDetected` is `false`, the field is backfilled to `root.last_updated` (best-approximation for pre-WP-005 ledgers). A single soft warning project comment (`type: 'warning'`, `priority: 'low'`, `agent: 'system'`) is emitted. Deduplication: the comment is only written if no identical note already exists (idempotent on repeated reads).
    27	
    28	2. **`ledger_version` backfill:** If `ledger_version` is absent, it is silently set to `SPEC_VERSION`. No comment is emitted — absence implies the ledger pre-dates versioning.
    29	
    30	3. **Forward-compatibility warning:** If `ledger_version` is present and its numeric major/minor/patch is strictly greater than `SPEC_VERSION`, a warning project comment is emitted — the server software may be older than the ledger it is reading. Deduplicated by note text.
    31	
    32	All repairs, the forward-compat check, pipeline ordering warnings, and the synthesis timestamp repair comment are consolidated into a single `withLock` scope. The pre-lock computation identifies which repairs are needed; inside the lock, each condition is re-checked against a fresh re-read (TOCTOU symmetry) and only applied if still true. This reduces lock acquisitions from 3 to 1 when multiple repairs fire simultaneously.
    33	
    34	The response JSON also includes a `pipeline_health` sub-object computed by reading all WP detail files:
    35	
    36	```typescript
    37	pipeline_health: {
    38	  wps_with_all_stages_pass: number;  // non-CANCELLED WPs with all active stages passing (uses wp.active_pipeline_stages.length ?? DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES.length)
    39	  wps_missing_stages: number;        // non-CANCELLED WPs with at least one stage missing
    40	  total_stages_missing: number;      // sum of missing stage counts across all wps_missing_stages WPs
    41	}
    42	```
    43	
    44	`CANCELLED` WPs are excluded from both `wps_with_all_stages_pass` and `wps_missing_stages`. Unreadable WP detail files are silently skipped — they contribute nothing to any count. This is a non-breaking additive field; consumers that do not expect it can ignore it.
    45	
    46	#### `ledger_initialize_project`
    47	
    48	```typescript
    49	(args: { 
    50	  project_path: string; 
    51	  plan_file: string;           // must equal 'plan.md' — enforced by Zod .refine()
    52	  project_summary?: string;    // min(1) — human-readable description of the project intent
    53	}) => Promise<MCPResult>
    54	```
    55	
    56	Creates a new project ledger with root index and centralized storage directory. Sets `ledger_version: SPEC_VERSION` on the root index at construction time. Rejects if ledger already exists. After writing the root index and project meta, copies `plan_file` into the centralized storage directory (best-effort). Response payload includes `archived_documents: string[]`, conditionally `archive_skipped: string[]` (omitted when empty), and `enrichment_cached: boolean` — `true` when step 5 meta enrichment (resolving project_name / repository_name) succeeded, `false` when it failed non-fatally. Enrichment failure is logged to stderr; the project is still created successfully.
    57	
    58	**`plan_file` constraint:** the `plan_file` argument is validated at parse time by a Zod `.refine()` check (`v === PLAN_ARCHIVE_FILENAME`). Any value other than `'plan.md'` is rejected with a validation error before handler logic runs. This ensures the GUI's `/api/projects/:slug/plan` endpoint can always rely on a fixed archive filename.
    59	
    60	**`project_summary` optional field:** When provided, the value is persisted to both `project-ledger.json` and `.meta.json` using key-presence semantics (the field is omitted entirely when not supplied — never written as `null`). The Zod `.min(1)` constraint rejects empty strings at parse time. In the GUI project detail page, `project_summary` is preferred over the auto-extracted synopsis (`extractSynopsis()` + `marked.parse()`): if set, the `.plan-synopsis` block renders it as XSS-safe plain text rather than Markdown. Bootstrapper agents should supply this field when creating a project, as it gives a curated, stable description that does not depend on plan file content.
    61	
    62	#### `ledger_list_projects`
    63	
    64	```typescript
    65	(args: {
    66	  status?: 'READY' | 'IN_PROGRESS' | 'COMPLETE' | 'BLOCKED' | 'ARCHIVED';
    67	  include_archived?: boolean;  // default: false
    68	}) => Promise<MCPResult>
    69	```
    70	
    71	Scans the central ledger root directory and returns metadata for all projects. Optionally filters by status. Projects with missing or invalid `.meta.json` are silently skipped.
    72	
    73	**ARCHIVED exclusion (default behavior):** When `include_archived` is `false` (the default), ARCHIVED projects are excluded from results unless an explicit `status: 'ARCHIVED'` filter is set. An explicit `status` filter always takes precedence — so `{ status: 'ARCHIVED' }` returns only archived projects regardless of `include_archived`. Pass `include_archived: true` to include archived projects alongside non-archived ones in an unfiltered listing.
    74	
    75	#### `ledger_complete_synthesis`
    76	
    77	```typescript
    78	(args: {
    79	  project_path?: string; // fallback — use only if already known from a previous tool response
    80	  cwd_path?: string; // preferred — auto-detects project
    81	  agent_role: string;
    82	  outcome_summary: string; // required — 2–3 sentence summary of what was accomplished
    83	  synthesis_file?: string;  // default: 'synthesis.md'
    84	}) => Promise<MCPResult>
    85	```
    86	
    87	Marks synthesis as generated on the root index. Sets `synthesis_generated = true` and `synthesis_generated_at = now()` (using the same timestamp for both the root index write and the response JSON), persists `outcome_summary` to both the root index (`project-ledger.json`) and the `.meta.json` enrichment cache, resets `auto_handoff_depth` to `0` (per §18.4), and transitions the project to `COMPLETE`. All writes are performed atomically within a single `withLock` callback. Called by the Synthesis agent (or Project Manager) after generating the final report. Copies `synthesis_file` into the centralized storage directory inside the lock scope (best-effort). Response payload includes `outcome_summary` (echoed back from the submitted value), `archived_documents: string[]`, and, conditionally, `archive_skipped: string[]` (omitted when empty).
    88	
    89	**`outcome_summary`** is a required string field — Zod rejects the call if it is absent or `null`. The value is written to `rootIndex.outcome_summary` and propagated to `.meta.json` via `writeRootIndex()` using key-presence semantics (`'outcome_summary' in validated`). The storage schema (`RootIndexSchema`) declares it as `z.string().nullable().optional()` for backward compatibility with legacy records that predate this field; the input schema (`CompleteSynthesisSchema`) enforces `z.string()` (required, non-nullable) so callers must always supply a value.
    90	
    91	**Required:** `agent_role` must be `"Synthesis"` or `"Project Manager"` — other roles receive an error.
    92	
    93	**§19.1 guards** (evaluated in order inside the lock):
    94	1. **Agent role guard** — rejects callers that are not `"Synthesis"` or `"Project Manager"`.
    95	2. **Fresh counter computation** — recomputes `totalWps` and `pendingWps` from the actual `work_packages` array (ignores stale `pending_work_packages` counter).
    96	3. **At-least-one-WP guard** — rejects calls on projects with no work packages.
    97	4. **Pending-WP guard** — rejects calls when `pendingWps > 0` (uses freshly computed value).
    98	
    99	All guards must pass before `synthesis_generated` is set. Not idempotent with respect to guard failures — a call with a pending WP or wrong role will return an error.
   100

   274	## �️ Cross-Platform Policy
   275	
   276	**Supported platforms:** Windows, macOS, and Linux. All sub-projects (MCP server, orchestrator, personas build system, root-level scripts) must work correctly on all three.
   277	
   278	### Rules
   279	
   280	1. **No OS-specific APIs without a cross-platform fallback.** When platform-specific code is unavoidable (e.g., file locking), provide per-platform implementations gated by runtime detection (`process.platform` / `sys.platform`) and document the invariants for each OS. Prefer stdlib-only solutions over third-party wrappers when the stdlib covers all three targets.

   282	3. **Shell commands must be cross-platform.** Root-level `scripts/` run on Node.js and must not rely on Unix-only utilities (e.g., `grep`, `sed`). Use Node.js built-in APIs or npm packages instead. When a script delegates to a shell, document any OS-specific invocation difference (e.g., venv activation).
   283	4. **File locking must work on all platforms.** The MCP server uses `proper-lockfile` (cross-platform). The orchestrator uses `src/utils/filelock.py` (`msvcrt` on Windows, `fcntl` on Unix). Any new locking mechanism must support all three OSs.
   284	5. **Tests must be platform-agnostic.** Avoid hardcoded Unix paths (`/tmp/…`) in test fixtures. Use the language's temp-directory API (`os.tmpdir()` / `tempfile.mkdtemp()`). Do not assert path separators — compare via `path.resolve()` or `pathlib` equivalents.
   285	6. **Line endings:** Rely on Git's `core.autocrlf` / `.gitattributes` for normalization. Never assume `\n` when reading user-edited files; use language-level line-splitting APIs.

   300	## �📝 Changelog Convention
   301	
   302	This workspace uses a **hub-and-spoke changelog model**: each sub-project maintains its own detailed changelog, and the root changelog aggregates the highlights into versioned releases.
   303	
   304	### File Locations
   305	
   306	| File | Scope | Versioning |
   307	|------|-------|------------|
   308	| `changelog.md` (root) | Workspace-wide release summary | SemVer, tagged in Git (`v1.9.0`, …) |
   309	| `mcp-server/changelog.md` | MCP server changes only | Own SemVer (`v1.14.0`, …), **not** Git-tagged |
   310	| `orchestrator/changelog.md` | Orchestrator changes only | Own SemVer (`v0.5.0`, …), **not** Git-tagged |
   311	| `personas/changelog.md` | Summary of the most relevant persona and build-system changes; individual persona changes are tracked in each persona's integrated changelog | Own SemVer (`v3.9.1`, …), **not** Git-tagged |
   312	
   313	### Rules
   314	
   315	1. **Only the root changelog triggers Git tags/releases.** Module changelogs track internal history but have no corresponding Git tags.
   316	2. **Module changelogs come first.** When preparing a release, update each affected module changelog before writing the root entry.
   317	3. **Root entries reference module versions.** Use the blockquote line format to link back: `> mcp v1.14.0 · personas v3.9.1 · orchestrator v0.4.0`. Omit modules that had no changes.
   318	4. **Root entries summarize, not duplicate.** Each root bullet condenses multiple module-level bullets into one outcome-oriented line. Implementation detail stays in the module changelog.
   319	5. **House style applies everywhere.** All changelogs follow the Changelog Curator's house style: flat bullet list with category prefixes, no `### Added/Changed/Fixed` sub-headers, ≤ 100-char lines.
   320	6. **Version bumps:** Root version follows SemVer based on the most significant change across all modules. Module versions are incremented independently.
   321	7. **`scripts/extract-changelog-entry.js`** parses the topmost root changelog entry for CI/GitHub Actions release automation.
   322	8. **Personas changelog is summary-only:** Since each persona has an integrated changelog, `personas/changelog.md` entries should summarize the most relevant changes per release — not list every individual per-persona change.

   326	```
   327	Step 1 — Module changelogs
   328	    For each module with changes since the last Git tag:

   331	
   332	Step 2 — Root changelog
   333	    → Read the new module entries
   334	    → Write a single new root entry summarizing the highlights
   335	    → Assign the next SemVer version
   336	```

101	#### `ledger_detect_project`
   102	
   103	```typescript
   104	(args: { cwd_path: string }) => Promise<MCPResult>
   105	```
   106	
   107	Identifies the active project by cross-referencing the supplied working-directory path against all project roots stored in the centralized ledger. Returns `{ plan_path, slug, title?, status }` for the unique matching project.
   108	
   109	**Error cases:**
   110	- **`NOT_FOUND`** — no known project root is an ancestor of `cwd_path`. Returned when `cwd_path` is not inside any initialized project's codebase.
   111	- **`AMBIGUOUS`** — more than one project root is an ancestor of `cwd_path`. The error message lists all matching `plan_path` values. Pass an explicit `project_path` to the tool requiring it to disambiguate.
   112	
   113	Note: `cwd_path` must be a directory path, not a file path. The tool does NOT require `project_path` as a parameter — that is the primary purpose of this tool.
   114	
   115	All tools (except `ledger_initialize_project`) now accept `cwd_path` directly — passing `cwd_path` to any tool triggers automatic project detection without needing a separate `ledger_detect_project` call. This tool remains available for standalone project detection when needed.
   116	
   117	#### `ledger_import_standalone`
   118	
   119	```typescript
   120	(args: {
   121	  project_path?: string;  // Absolute path to the standalone plan folder to import. Takes precedence over cwd_path.
   122	  cwd_path?: string;      // Alternative plan folder path. Used when project_path is not provided.
   123	  // At least one of project_path or cwd_path is required.
   124	  project_summary?: string; // Optional. Curated 2–3 sentence plain-text description. min(1). Whitespace-only strings pass validation but are not useful.
   125	}) => Promise<MCPResult>
   126	```
   127	
   128	Imports a completed standalone developer plan execution into the project ledger. Designed for use after a standalone (non-ledger-workflow) development session where the developer used the Standalone Developer persona and produced a `plan.md` and `synthesis.md`.
   129	
   130	**Validation rules (evaluated in order):**
   131	1. **Path required** — rejects calls that supply neither `project_path` nor `cwd_path`.
   132	2. **Plan folder naming** — the folder basename must match the `{YYYY-MM-DD}-{name}` convention (validated by `planFolderBasename()`). Returns a descriptive error on mismatch.
   133	3. **`plan.md` existence** — rejects with `"Import failed: plan.md not found in …"` when the file is absent.
   134	4. **`synthesis.md` existence** — rejects with `"Import failed: synthesis.md not found in …"` when the file is absent.

Tool code calls no `@internal` storage primitives directly (Constraint 2c).
   144	
   145	**Produced project record:**
   146	- `project-ledger.json`: `status: 'COMPLETE'`, `total_work_packages: 1`, `pending_work_packages: 0`, `synthesis_generated: true`, `runner: 'standalone'`, `outcome_summary` populated, `project_summary` included when provided (omitted when not supplied — key-presence semantics).
   147	- `WP-001.json`: `status: 'COMPLETE'`, `assigned_to: 'Developer'`, `active_pipeline_stages: ['implementation']`, single `implementation` pipeline at `PASS`.
   148	- `.meta.json`: auto-synced by `writeRootIndex()` inside the lock.
   149	- `plan.md` and `synthesis.md` archived to `{ledgerRoot}/{repoName}/{slug}/`.
   150	
   151	**Response shape (on success):**
   152	
   153	```typescript
   154	{
   155	  slug: string;                // Plan folder basename (e.g. "2026-06-30-my-feature")
   156	  outcome_summary: string | null; // Extracted from synthesis.md; null when not found
   157	  archived_files: string[];    // Filenames successfully copied to storage dir

   159	}

   165	
   166	#### `ledger_update_synthesis`
   167	
   168	```typescript
   169	(args: {
   170	  project_path?: string;  // Absolute path to the standalone plan folder. Takes precedence over cwd_path.
   171	  cwd_path?: string;      // Alternative plan folder path. Used when project_path is not provided.
   172	  // At least one of project_path or cwd_path is required.
   173	}) => Promise<MCPResult>
   174	```

   178	**Guards (evaluated in order):**

   102	| `stage_complete` | Agent stage finished successfully — carries `tokens_used`, `duration_s` |
   103	| `route` | Supervisor routing decision — carries `destination`, `reason` (all entries); `prev_stage`, `prev_result`, `agent_role`, `ledger_action` (WP-routing entries only) |
   104	| `progress_snapshot` | Periodic status — carries `status_breakdown`, `pending`, `elapsed_s` |

   109	| `wp_complete` | WP reached COMPLETE |
   110	| `pipeline_result` | Pipeline outcome — carries `pipeline_status`, `files_modified`, `summary` |
   111	
   112	### Chunk File Format (JSONL)
   113	
   114	Each chunk file captures the raw LangGraph `AIMessageChunk` stream for one stage run.
   115	
   116	- **Line 1 (header):** `{"chunk_format": 1, "stream_mode": "messages", "langgraph_stream_version": "v2"}`
   117	- **Subsequent lines:** `{"ns": [...], "msg": {...}, "metadata": {...}}`
   118	
   119	Key fields in chunk lines:
   120	
   121	| Field | Description |
   122	|-------|-------------|
   123	| `ns` | Namespace array — identifies the agent and sub-agent (e.g., `["developer:UUID"]`) |
   124	| `msg.content` | Array of content blocks — `text` type for prose, `tool_use` type for tool calls, `input_json_delta` for streaming JSON arguments |
   125	| `msg.type` | Always `"AIMessageChunk"` |
   126	| `msg.tool_calls` | Parsed tool calls (when complete) |
   127	| `msg.invalid_tool_calls` | Tool calls that failed parsing — diagnostic signal for agent confusion |
   128	| `msg.usage_metadata` | Token usage (typically on the final chunk of a response) |
   129	| `metadata.ls_model_name` | Model used for this chunk |
   130	| `metadata.langgraph_step` | Step counter within the graph |
   131	| `metadata.langgraph_node` | Active graph node |
   132	| `metadata.langgraph_checkpoint_ns` | Checkpoint namespace for resume tracing |
   133	| `metadata.lc_versions` | Library versions (e.g., `{"deepagents": "…", "langchain_core": "…"}` — keys use underscores) |
   134	
   135	### Diagnostic Signals in Chunks
   136	
   137	- **`invalid_tool_calls`** with non-null entries → agent produced malformed tool invocations (JSON parsing failures, hallucinated tool names)
   138	- **Repeated identical tool calls** in sequence → agent is stuck in a loop
   139	- **Very large `input_json_delta` sequences** for a single argument → agent is generating excessively verbose tool inputs
   140	- **Text content between tool calls** that describes confusion, backtracking, or self-correction → agent encountered unexpected state
   141	- **Missing chunk files** for expected stages → stage crashed before dialogue capture or capture was suppressed
   142	
   143	---
   144	
   145	## Evaluation Criteria
   146	
   147	Classify each finding along these dimensions:
   148	
   149	| Dimension | Description |
   150	|-----------|-------------|
   151	| **Severity** | Critical (run failed / data loss), Major (WP reworked / halted), Minor (inefficiency / cosmetic) |
   152	| **Category** | See Finding Categories below |
   153	| **Scope** | Isolated (one WP/stage) vs. Systemic (recurring pattern) |
   154	| **Root Cause Layer** | Orchestrator infrastructure, MCP server, agent persona, LangGraph/Deep Agents runtime, or external (API provider) |
   155	
   156	### Finding Categories
   157	
   158	| Category | Examples |
   159	|----------|---------|
   160	| **Agent Errors** | Stage crashes, unhandled exceptions, malformed tool calls |
   161	| **Routing Anomalies** | Unexpected routing decisions, rework loops, premature halts |
   162	| **Performance Issues** | Excessive stage duration, token waste, heartbeat stalls |
   163	| **MCP Friction** | Tool errors, repeated failed tool calls, schema mismatches |
   164	| **Virtualization Artifacts** | LangGraph-specific issues — checkpoint failures, stream interruptions, Deep Agents backend errors |
   165	| **Persona Compliance** | Agent deviating from its persona instructions (visible in chunk dialogue) |
   166	
   167	---
   168	
   169	## Output Template

   103

   111	
   112	## 1.X Server-side TypeScript Modules
   113	
   114	### `chunk-accumulator.ts` — Shared accumulation layer
   115	
   116	Pure-function module. No I/O, no side effects, no imports from `mcp-server/src/`. All exports are named.
   117	
   118	#### Types
   119	
   120	| Export | Kind | Description |
   121	|--------|------|-------------|
   122	| `JsonValue` | `type` | Raw JSON value accepted in chunk payloads. |
   123	| `ToolCallChunk` | `interface` | Single tool-call fragment from an `AIMessageChunk`. Fields: `index?`, `id?`, `name?`, `args?`. |
   124	| `MergedToolCall` | `interface` | Accumulated tool call (after merging). Fields: `id`, `name`, `args`. |
   125	| `ContentBlock` | `interface` | Content block (text or non-text). Fields: `type`, `text?`, index signature. |
   126	| `MergedMessage` | `interface` | Merged/reconstructed message. Fields: `type`, `id`, `content`, `tool_calls`, `usage_metadata`, `tool_call_id?`. |
   127	| `NamespaceKey` | `type` | `string` — `""` for main agent, `"subgraph/node"` for sub-agents. |
   128	
   129	#### Functions
   130	
   131	| Export | Signature | Description |
   132	|--------|-----------|-------------|
   133	| `chunkId` | `(chunk: Record<string, JsonValue>) → string` | Extracts the stable `id` field from a chunk payload. |
   134	| `chunkType` | `(chunk: Record<string, JsonValue>) → string` | Returns the `type` field from a chunk payload. |
   135	| `mergeContent` | `(acc, incoming) → string \| ContentBlock[]` | Merges a new content value into an accumulated content value (string concat or block-list merge). |
   136	| `mergeToolCallChunks` | `(acc: Map<number, MergedToolCall>, chunks: ToolCallChunk[]) → void` | Merges `tool_call_chunks` fragments into an accumulator map keyed by index. |
   137	| `mergeUsageMetadata` | `(acc, incoming) → Record<string, number>` | Sums `usage_metadata` numeric fields into an accumulator. |
   138	| `isValidHeader` | `(line: string) → boolean` | Validates that a JSONL line is a `chunk_format: 1` header. |
   139	| `parseChunkLine` | `(line: string) → { namespace, msg, metadata } \| null` | Parses one JSONL data line (object or array shape). Returns `null` on parse errors. |
   140	| `namespaceKey` | `(ns: string[]) → NamespaceKey` | Converts a raw namespace array to a display key (`""` for main agent). |
   141	| `namespaceLabel` | `(key: NamespaceKey) → string` | Returns a human-readable label (`"Main Agent"` or the key string). |
   142	| `accumulateChunks` | `(records: Array<{ namespace, msg }>) → Map<NamespaceKey, MergedMessage[]>` | Accumulates parsed chunk records into a namespace-keyed map of merged messages. |
   143	
   144	### `chunk-renderer.ts` — Rendering layer
   145	
   146	Imports all types and functions from `chunk-accumulator.ts`. Exports four pure renderers and the `DialogueBlock` discriminated union type:
   147	
   148	| Export | Signature | Description |
   149	|--------|-----------|-------------|
   150	| `renderChunksToMarkdown` | `(jsonlContent: string) → string` | Verbose format: `## Role` headings, JSON fenced tool-call blocks, token-usage footer. |
   151	| `renderChunksToDialogue` | `(jsonlContent: string) → string` | Compact chat-like format: plain-paragraph AI text, per-tool summary lines, hidden ToolMessages, sub-agent `### Subagent:` headings. |
   152	| `renderChunksToStructured` | `(jsonlContent: string) → DialogueBlock[]` | Structured format: returns a typed JSON array of `DialogueBlock` objects for interactive frontend rendering. |
   153	| `renderChunksToText` | `(jsonlContent: string) → string` | Prose-only extraction: AI text turns only, no tool-call JSON, no tool results. Single-namespace files render as flat prose; multi-namespace files get `## Outer Agent` / `## Inner Agent` section headers (one per inner namespace, all labeled identically). Returns `'*No dialogue recorded.*\n'` for empty or content-free input. Shares its `.md` output format with `scripts/extract-dialogue.js`. |
   154	| `DialogueBlock` | *(exported type)* | Discriminated union describing one rendered block in the structured view. |
   155	
   156	#### `DialogueBlock` Type
   157	
   158	```typescript
   159	type DialogueBlock =
   160	  | { type: 'text'; content: string }
   161	  | { type: 'tool-call'; name: string; detailLines: string[]; args: unknown; result?: { content: string } }
   162	  | { type: 'subagent-heading'; label: string }
   163	  | { type: 'checklist'; items: Array<{ content: string; status: string; checked: boolean }> };
   164	```
   165	
   166	Variants:
   167	- `text` — A prose paragraph of AI-generated text.
   168	- `tool-call` — One tool invocation: name, summary detail lines, parsed args JSON, and an optional embedded ToolMessage result for non-inline tools (e.g. `read_file`, `ledger_*`).
   169	- `subagent-heading` — Heading marking the start of a sub-agent namespace.
   170	- `checklist` — A `write_todos` invocation rendered as a typed item list; each item carries `content`, `status`, and a pre-computed `checked` boolean.

   173	
   174	## 2. Frontend Global Namespaces
   175	
   176	### 2.1 `API` (api-client.js)
   177	
   178	Client-side REST API wrapper. All methods return Promises.
   179

   181	|--------|-----------|----------|
